title: Learning to read, WPA band, and marriage at sixteen
summary: He says he is a builder like his father, learned to read from Richard McClain, Pinchback and Wilcox, and could not get on the WPA band. He says his wife came from the same neighbourhood and that they married when he was sixteen and she fifteen.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Well, there's only another minute or so left. Is there anything else you'd like to tell about your life that you can think of? Well... Or your playing, your music, anything at all?
Well, I think a lot of playing and music, you know, I really like music. I'm a builder. My father was a builder. Yes, you do. And then I stepped in on that, you know, from a kid too.
You say some of these men helped you to read, so you learned to read music then too?

Yes, yes. Well, the first one really learned me how to... I had been, you know, spelling a little bit and Richard McClane, he started me reading. And then I got with Pinchback and he showed me the rest. And then I goes on to this guy, Wilcox, and he showed me some about reading, so that's how I learned how to read. Did you ever find that big WPA band they had during the... No, I, no, no, I couldn't get on the WPA. They wouldn't ever put me on. No. No, they wouldn't put me in that band. And a lot of musicians. Yeah, they had a lot of them, but you had to, you had to pull some straws to get in that thing. Yeah. Yeah, you could, I couldn't get in it.
Your wife came from downtown, you're saying you moved downtown later.
No, no, my wife came, we came from around the same place. Yeah. See, I got married when I was 16. Oh, that early. Yeah, I got married when I was 16. She was 15, I was 16.
